questions.question: Ranjan covered a total distance of 108 km at an average speed of 12 km. he covers (1)/(6)th of total distance in 2 hours while (1)/(4)th of the total distance at a speed of 9 km/h. In how much time did he cover the remaining distance?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total distance covered by Ranjan = 108 km

Average speed = 12 km/h

He covers (1/6)th of total distance in 2 hours

He covers (1/4)th of the total distance at a speed of 9 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance / Speed

**Calculation:**

Distance covered in the first part = (1/6) × 108 km = 18 km

Time taken for the first part = 2 hours

Distance covered in the second part = (1/4) × 108 km = 27 km

Speed for the second part = 9 km/h

Time taken for the second part ⇒ Time = Distance / Speed

Time taken for the second part ⇒ Time = 27 / 9 = 3 hours

Let time taken to cover the remaining distance = x

Average speed = 12 km/h = Total distance/ Total time

⇒ 12 = 108/(2 + 3 + x)

⇒ 12(5 + x) = 108

⇒ x = (108 - 60)/12 = 4

**The correct answer is option 3: 4 hours**

questions.question: If (sec θ-tan θ)/(sec θ+tan θ)=(1)/(7), θ lies in first quadrant, then the value of (cosec theta+cot² theta)/(cosec theta-cot² theta) is:

By Componendo and Dividendo: sec θ / tan θ = (7 + 1) / (7 − 1) = 8 / 6 = 4 / 3.

Since sec θ / tan θ = (1/cos θ) / (sin θ/cos θ) = 1/sin θ = cosec θ.

∴ cosec θ = 4/3 and cot² θ = cosec² θ − 1 = (4/3)² − 1 = 7/9.

Required value = (4/3 + 7/9) / (4/3 − 7/9) = (19/9) / (5/9) = 19/5.

**∴ The correct answer is 19/5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (sec θ − tan θ) / (sec θ + tan θ) = 1/7

**Formula Used:** Componendo and Dividendo: If a/b = c/d, then (b+a)/(b-a) = (d+c)/(d-c). Also, cosec² θ − cot² θ = 1.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/865866ff264c3a6811fffa8f3a52bb53dba77aaf7f22a8c3972a500a21000e26.png] 

⇒ (sec θ − tan θ) / (sec θ + tan θ) = 1/7

⇒ [(sec θ + tan θ) + (sec θ − tan θ)] / [(sec θ + tan θ) − (sec θ − tan θ)] = (7 + 1) / (7 − 1)

⇒ (2 sec θ) / (2 tan θ) = 8 / 6

⇒ (1/cos θ) × (cos θ/sin θ) = 4 / 3

⇒ 1/sin θ = cosec θ = 4 / 3

⇒ cot² θ = cosec² θ − 1 = (4/3)² − 1 = 16/9 − 1 = 7/9

⇒ Value = (cosec θ + cot² θ) / (cosec θ − cot² θ)

⇒ Value = (4/3 + 7/9) / (4/3 − 7/9)

⇒ Value = [(12 + 7) / 9] / [(12 − 7) / 9] = 19 / 5

**∴ The correct answer is 19/5.**

Componendo and Dividendo Rule

If the ratio a/b = c/d, then (a + b) / (a − b) = (c + d) / (c − d). This is very useful in simplifying trigonometric fractions.

questions.question: A person buys the stock of a company at Rs. 12,000. If he sells that stock (a year later) he gets Rs. 15,000. Determine the percentage profit earned.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Purchase price of stock = Rs. 12,000

Selling price of stock = Rs. 15,000

**Concept used: **

Calculation of profit percentage = (Profit/Cost Price) x 100%

**Solution:**

Profit = Selling Price - Cost Price = Rs. 15,000 - Rs. 12,000 = Rs. 3,000

Profit Percentage = (Profit / Cost Price) x 100% = (Rs. 3,000 / Rs. 12,000) x 100% = 25%

**Therefore, the percentage profit earned is 25%.**

questions.question: X, Y and Z invest capitals in the ratio 18 ∶ 20 ∶ 25. After 6 months, X increases his capital by 33(1)/(3)\% and Y decreases his capital by 50% and no change in the capital of Z. What is the share of Y in the profit of Rs. 15.25 lakhs at the end of a year?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit ratio = (Capital × Time)

Equiv. Capital → X = (18 × 6) + (24 × 6) = 252 | Y = (20 × 6) + (10 × 6) = 180 | Z = 25 × 12 = 300

Profit Ratio = 252 : 180 : 300 = 21 : 15 : 25 (Total = 61 parts)

Y's Share = (15 ÷ 61) × 15,25,000 = 3,75,000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 3,75,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of initial capitals of X, Y, and Z = 18 : 20 : 25

Total profit at the end of a year = Rs. 15.25 lakhs = Rs. 15,25,000

**Formula Used:**

Profit Ratio = (C₁ × T₁) : (C₂ × T₂) : (C₃ × T₃)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7459729b2e1e6a074d7f5759f857f0367e727483acaaf66d72ca50c9b30e97eb.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial capitals be 18k, 20k, and 25k respectively.

⇒ After 6 months, X increases his capital by 33(1/3)% = 1/3.

⇒ New capital of X = 18k + (1/3 × 18k) = 18k + 6k = 24k

⇒ After 6 months, Y decreases his capital by 50% = 1/2.

⇒ New capital of Y = 20k − (1/2 × 20k) = 20k − 10k = 10k

⇒ Z's capital remains unchanged for 12 months.

⇒ X's equivalent capital for 12 months = (18k × 6) + (24k × 6) = 108k + 144k = 252k

⇒ Y's equivalent capital for 12 months = (20k × 6) + (10k × 6) = 120k + 60k = 180k

⇒ Z's equivalent capital for 12 months = 25k × 12 = 300k

⇒ Ratio of their shares in profit = 252k : 180k : 300k

⇒ Dividing by 12k, we get the simplified ratio = 21 : 15 : 25

⇒ Sum of the ratio terms = 21 + 15 + 25 = 61

⇒ Share of Y in profit = (15 ÷ 61) × 15,25,000

⇒ Y's Share = 15 × 25,000 = Rs. 3,75,000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 3,75,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Partnership

If partners invest their capitals for the same duration, profits are divided strictly in the ratio of their investments (C₁ : C₂ : C₃).

Compound Partnership

When investments are for different time periods, the profit ratio is the product of capital and time: (C₁ × T₁) : (C₂ × T₂) : (C₃ × T₃).

Working vs Sleeping Partner

A working partner receives a fixed salary or a specific percentage of the profit for managing the business. The remaining profit is then shared based on their investment ratios.

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an example of **Direct Speech**.
 
• In order to convert the Direct Narration into an Indirect sentence, we need to go through the following steps:
 
 
• Change the reporting verb '***said to***' to the same tense and verb aspect of '**tell**'.
 
• Insert '***that***' before the statement.
 
• Remove the comma and the inverted commas that border the direct speech.
 
• As subject perspective changes, change '***my dog***' to '***her dog***.'
 
• 'Change the verb '***doesn't like***' to '***didn't like***'.
 
 
 
• **Correct Sentence: **'*Sanjana told me that her dog didn't like the postman.*'

__
 
• **Direct Speech**- a report or quote of the exact words used by a speaker or writer.
 
• **Indirect Speech**- speech that tells you what someone said, but does not use the person's actual words or the speech marks.
 
• **Reporting verb**- a verb that is used to talk about or report on other people's work.
 
• **say **and **tell** ⇒ In the indirect speech, '**say**' is most often used without a personal object (if a personal object is necessary) whereas '**tell**' normally has a personal object. For example,
 
 
• '*Kamalika said she would be late*.'

questions.question:
Change the following sentence into indirect speech:

Tom said, "I woke up feeling ill, so I didn't go to work."

options.text: Tom said that he woke up feeling ill and so he did not go to work.
Tom said that he had woken up feeling ill, so he hadn't gone to work.
Tom said that he had woken up feeling ill, so he did not go to work.
Tom said that he woke up feeling ill, so he didn't go to work.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Option 2".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When reporting speech in English, the tense of the verb is usually moved back in 'sequence of tenses'. 
 
• The simple past tense **('woke up')** is usually changed into the past perfect tense** ('had woken up').**
 
• Similarly, **"didn't go"** should correctly change to "**hadn't gone".** 
 
• This falls under the rule of backshifting where a** past simple** ('did not go') **converts to past perfect** ('had not gone') in reported speech.
 
• The **rest of the sentence** (the conjunction 'so' and the subject 'he') **remains unchanged** in indirect speech.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: 'Tom said that he had woken up feeling ill, so he hadn't gone to work.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The cell wall is responsible for maintaining the turgidity of the cell.**__
 
• The cell wall is a rigid layer that surrounds the cell membrane of plant cells, bacteria, and some fungi.
 
• The cell wall is made up of cellulose, hemicellulose, and pectin.
 
• Cell walls are a feature of almost all prokaryotic cells, as well as many eukaryotic organisms.
 
• In addition to providing structural support and maintaining the shape of the cell, The cell wall serves as a protective barrier against physical and biological threats.
 
• It also allows the cell to withstand the difference in osmotic pressure between the cell's interior and its environment.
 
• However, it is not primarily involved in functions such as storage of material, cell division, or the synthesis of carbohydrates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__****Lysosomes**

__
 
• **Lysosomes **are small, spherical, sac-like structures that contain several digestive enzymes enclosed in a membrane.
 
• They help in the digestion of foreign substances and worn-out cell organelles.__
 
• They protect against bacteria and viruses.
 
• They help to keep the cell clean.
 
• During the disturbance in cellular metabolism, for example, when the cell gets damaged, lysosomes may burst and the enzymes digest their own cell.
 
• Therefore, lysosomes are also known as suicide bags of a cell.

**Plastids**

 
• Plastids are responsible for photosynthesis, storage of products like starch, and the synthesis of many classes of molecules such as fatty acids and terpenes, which are needed as cellular building blocks and/or for the function of the plant.
 
• There are different types of plastids with their specialized functions.

**Golgi Body**

 
• A major function of Golgi bodies is the modification of proteins.
 
• It is a major organelle in most eukaryotic cells.
 
• It has the structure of membrane-bound sacs.
 
• Its function is to process and package the macromolecules such as proteins and lipids that are synthesized by the cell.
 
• Its functions also involve the transport of lipids around the cell and the creation of lysosomes.
 
• The sacs/folds of the Golgi apparatus are called cisternae.
 
• The Golgi complex works jointly with the rough endoplasmic reticulum.
 
• When the endoplasmic reticulum makes a protein, a transition vesicle is also made later it drifts through the cytoplasm to the Golgi apparatus where it gets absorbed.
 
• After the Golgi works on the molecules inside, it secretes a vesicle into the cytoplasm which then releases the protein molecule out of the cell.

__
 
• The concept of judicial review in the Indian Constitution is derived from the Constitution of the **United States of America (USA).**
 
• Judicial review refers to the power of the judiciary to interpret the constitutionality of laws and executive actions.
 
• In the USA, the concept was established in the landmark case of **Marbury v. Madison** (1803).
 
• It ensures that the laws passed by the legislature and actions taken by the executive are in accordance with the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Judicial Review**

 
 
• It is a process under which executive or legislative actions are subject to review by the judiciary.
 
• It is an essential function of the judiciary to safeguard the supremacy of the Constitution and to protect the fundamental rights of citizens.
 
• In India, judicial review is considered a basic feature of the Constitution, which cannot be amended or taken away by the Parliament.
 
• Articles 32 and 226 of the Indian Constitution provide the basis for judicial review of legislative and executive actions.
 
 
 
• **Marbury v. Madison (1803)**
 
 
• This case is significant in American constitutional history as it established the principle of judicial review in the United States.
 
• The case was decided by the Supreme Court under Chief Justice John Marshall.
 
• The ruling declared that the Supreme Court had the power to nullify an act of Congress if it was found to be in conflict with the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Indian Constitution and Judicial Review**
 
 
• The Indian Constitution explicitly confers the power of judicial review on the judiciary through Articles 13, 32, 131-136, 143, 226, and 246.
 
• The Constitution of India provides a system of checks and balances to ensure that no organ of the government exceeds its powers.
 
• Judicial review in India plays a critical role in maintaining the rule of law and ensuring the protection of fundamental rights.
